perspective:
From Christian Mensah’s subjective perspective, the available information is:

- He is a police officer and Jonathan Balogun is his childhood/best friend. Christian often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his perspective.
- Scenario 1: Christian had been feeling anxious and suspicious that Jonathan was hiding something important. He arranged a meeting at their favorite coffee shop and confronted Jonathan. Christian heard Jonathan admit that he had been hiding something: Jonathan is in some trouble and did not know how to tell him.
- Scenario 2: Christian felt worried and empathetic. He offered to help and said they could face it together. Jonathan told him the situation is complicated and he did not want to drag Christian into it. Jonathan also said he could use support and resources and needs to find a way out of the mess.
- Scenario 3: Christian came to believe Jonathan’s trouble might be related to criminal activity, and felt conflicted and concerned. He asked Jonathan if it was illegal. Jonathan said he could not say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he did not do anything illegal himself. Christian said he would look into it discreetly without alarming Jonathan. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Scenario 4: Through his own investigation, Christian came to believe Jonathan is being framed and that someone is trying to set him up. He told Jonathan this. Christian did not yet know who was responsible, but he had leads. He decided to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence. Jonathan thanked him and said he did not know what he would do without him.
- Scenario 5: Christian came to believe the real culprit is someone close to both him and Jonathan, someone they both know and trust. He felt betrayed and resolute. He told Jonathan he had found out who was behind it, but in the provided dialogue he only tells Jonathan that it is someone close to them. Christian decided to confront the culprit and bring them to justice. Jonathan warned him the person is dangerous, but said he trusted Christian to do what is right.

Christian does not have access to any hidden facts beyond what he personally observed, was told, or learned through his own investigation.
